key_insight: A minimizing-movement framework uses a convex energy surrogate to construct parametric finite element schemes for anisotropic curve shortening with provable one-step energy dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports energy-consistent simulation of evolving interfaces, including anisotropic and area-preserving motion.
method: Majorize the anisotropic energy with a smooth, convex surrogate that matches it at the current iterate.
Solve a uniquely solvable unconstrained step for any positive time-step size, provided the current curve has nonvanishing elementwise parametric derivatives.
Use convex splitting for strong anisotropy and a scalar constraint for area preservation.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show approximately expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic cases, energy dissipation, and area preservation.
watch_item: Strongly anisotropic simulations develop sharp facet-like profiles but exhibit mesh-scale oscillations under grid refinement.
paper_title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
